title: Determination of the real-life validity of the Lolli-Method for the detection of RSV, Influenza and SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) in the pediatric emergency department
summary: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and influenza pose a significant health risk to children under the age of five. Early and accurate diagnosis through the analysis of respiratory samples is crucial for effective infection control and treatment. The minimally invasive Lolli-Method, in which children suck on a swab for 30 seconds, which is then examined using a PCR test, offers a simple and child-friendly alternative to conventional nasal/pharyngeal swabs. A recent study shows that the lollipop method has a sensitivity of 100% for the detection of acute RSV and influenza infections in children. Based on these results, the Lolli-Method will be introduced as standard sampling in the pediatric emergency room at the University Hospital of Cologne from the 2024/2025 RSV season. The implementation will be accompanied by a quality assurance program to ensure optimal care and infection protection. The aim of the study is to confirm the real-world validity of the Lolli-Method in clinical practice.
conditions: Respiratory syncytial virus as the cause of diseases classified to other chapters

interventions.name: Currently, children in the pediatric emergency department are routinely sampled using a nasal/throat swab and tested for RSV, Influenza and SARS-CoV-2 using a point-of-care PCR-test. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patient at the Clinic and Polyclinic for Pediatrics and Adolescent Medicine at the University Hospital of Cologne
- Testing carried out for RSV, influenza and SARS-CoV-2 as part of the routine care of the Clinic and Polyclinic for Pediatrics and Adolescent Medicine at the University Hospital of Cologne
Exclusion criteria:
- Not a patient of the Clinic and Polyclinic for Pediatrics and Adolescent Medicine at the University Hospital of Cologne
- No testing for RSV, influenza and SARS-CoV-2 carried out as part of the routine care of the Clinic and Polyclinic for Pediatrics and Adolescent Medicine at the University Hospital of Cologne
